sources.entry: Local Content Share - Store and share text snippets and files within your local network. MIT Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted app for sharing text snippets, files, and links across a local network with no client-side setup, and a built-in Markdown notepad.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you store and share text snippets, uploaded files, and links with any device on your local network through a web browser, with no client software needed. Snippets can be created, renamed, edited, viewed, and copied, and files can be uploaded (including multiple files via drag-and-drop or paste), downloaded, renamed, and deleted. Each item can have an expiration of Never, 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, or a custom value such as 3w or 2M, and a DEFAULT_EXPIRY environment variable can set the default. Links are listed in last-in, first-shown order, and a Notepad supports Markdown editing and preview with autosave. The UI pushes live updates to all connected clients using SSE, and the frontend works offline with local assets and as a PWA.
use_cases: share text snippets between devices on a home network
temporarily host files for others on the LAN
quick paste of text or screenshots from a phone to a computer
keep a shared scratchpad or Markdown notes accessible from any device
store and share a list of useful links
AirDrop-style transfer between devices without cloud services
how_to_run: git clone the repository, cd local-content-share, then go build .
notable: Automatic per-item expiration (TTL) with cycling presets and custom durations
Multi-file drag-and-drop upload and clipboard paste of files or screenshots
Real-time updates to all clients via SSE
Works fully offline with local assets and can be installed as a PWA
Single binary or Docker image, with a data directory that holds files, snippets, notes, and expiration.json
caveats: No authentication is implemented; the README says it is meant only for the homelab and must be placed behind auth if exposed publicly
Reverse proxies may impose upload size limits or buffer uploads, so extra settings (for example, Nginx Proxy Manager custom config) may be needed
